ai.description: *Smithophis atemporalis* is a slender snake reaching 60 cm. It is dark brown dorsally with a yellow underside and lacks temporal scales. A distinctive pale collar marks the neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Smithophis atemporalis* is uniquely distinguished from similar Indian natricids by the complete absence of temporal scales, causing the parietals to border the labials.
ai.habitat: *Smithophis atemporalis* inhabits moist evergreen forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Smithophis atemporalis* is primarily diurnal, often foraging for small amphibians and fish in or near shallow, slow-moving streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Smithophis atemporalis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August in Northeast India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Smithophis atemporalis* is endemic to the mid-elevation forests of the Northeast Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.
